symptoms_to_check: Dark brown to black circular to angular sunken lesions on leaves.
Shot-hole effect where brittle dead lesion centers dry out and drop.
Blossom blight and black necrotic spots on young panicles.
immediate_actions: Prune and safely burn infected twigs and mummified panicles.
Rake and remove fallen infected leaves from beneath the tree canopy to reduce spore reservoir.
Avoid overhead irrigation during new leaf flush and flowering.
preventive_measures: Maintain open tree canopy architecture via annual pruning for rapid leaf drying.
Avoid high-nitrogen fertilizer applications during flushes which produce overly succulent susceptible foliage.
Ensure proper orchard drainage to lower microclimate humidity.
treatment_options: Preventive copper oxychloride (3 g/L) spray at the onset of new vegetative flush.
Systemic foliar spray such as Azoxystrobin (1 ml/L) or Carbendazim (1 g/L) if disease pressure is high.
Repeat treatments at 14-day intervals during warm humid conditions adhering strictly to label rates.
Anthracnose.when_to_seek_expert_help: Consult local agricultural extension if black necrotic lesions spread rapidly to flower panicles and young fruit sets.

sources.title: Mango Diseases and Their Management
sources.organization: ICAR - Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture

Bacterial Canker.display_name: Mango Bacterial Canker (Xanthomonas citri pv. mangiferaeindicae)
symptoms_to_check: Water-soaked angular lesions bounded by leaf veins that turn raised, black, and cankerous.
Prominent chlorotic yellow halos encircling the dark lesions.
Longitudinal cracks on twigs and gummy bacterial exudate oozing from lesions.
immediate_actions: Prune out infected twigs 10 cm below lesion margin using shears sterilized in 70% alcohol or 10% bleach.
Collect and incinerate all diseased prunings and fallen diseased leaves.
Avoid working in the orchard when canopy is wet to prevent mechanical transmission.
preventive_measures: Establish protective windbreaks around the orchard perimeter to minimize wind-driven leaf abrasion.
Inspect nursery graft material rigorously before field planting.
Disinfect harvesting and pruning equipment between trees.
treatment_options: Bactericidal spray of Copper Oxychloride (2.5 g/L) mixed with Streptomycin Sulfate (100 ppm / 0.1 g/L).
Apply at bud emergence and repeat every 15-20 days during rainy monsoon periods.
Rotate bactericidal modes of action to manage resistance.
Bacterial Canker.when_to_seek_expert_help: Seek professional diagnosis if cankers show extensive bacterial gumming on major scaffolds or young fruit sets.

sources.title: Mango Canker Management
sources.organization: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research

symptoms_to_check: Clean, scissor-like transverse incisions across tender young leaves.
Severed apical halves of leaves hanging limp or littering the ground under the canopy.
Tiny adult weevils (reddish-brown with long snouts) visible on fresh flush.
immediate_actions: Collect and destroy severed leaf tips containing oviposited eggs lying on the ground.
Gently shake affected young branches over a white cloth in early morning to dislodge and capture adults.
Apply sticky tree trunk barrier bands to impede crawling insects.
preventive_measures: Shallow basin hoeing and raking under the tree dripline to expose pupae to sun and avian predators.
Synchronize tree flushes with balanced nutrition to shorten vulnerable tender-flush windows.
treatment_options: Foliar application of Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) or Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm at 2 ml/L) on new flush.
If infestation exceeds 10% severed foliage, apply contact bio-rational insecticide such as Deltamethrin (0.5 ml/L) per local label.
Cutting Weevil.when_to_seek_expert_help: Call extension officers if more than 30% of the terminal vegetative flush in young non-bearing trees is severed.

sources.title: Insect Pests of Mango and Their Control
sources.organization: Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine & Storage

symptoms_to_check: Leaves on terminal shoots turn brown, roll inward, and desiccate without falling.
Discoloration and die-back progressing downward from the twig tip toward larger branches.
Vascular cambium under the bark turns brown to purplish-black when scraped.
immediate_actions: Prune dying twigs 8-10 cm below the lowest visible margin of discoloration into sound green wood.
Immediately seal all cut wound surfaces with Bordeaux paste or Copper Oxychloride slurry.
Burn or bury all pruned infected wood outside the grove perimeter.
preventive_measures: Control stem borers and wood-boring insects whose exit wounds serve as entry points for the fungal pathogen.
Avoid water stress and heavy salinity spikes during dry post-monsoon and summer periods.
Ensure zinc and micronutrient balance to strengthen woody tissue defenses.
treatment_options: Foliar spray of Thiophanate-Methyl (1 g/L) or Carbendazim (1 g/L) following pruning operations.
Drench soil root zone with Copper Oxychloride (3 g/L) in severely affected orchards.
Die Back.when_to_seek_expert_help: Contact an agronomist if die-back spreads into primary scaffold limbs or main tree trunk.

sources.title: Management of Mango Dieback and Decline

symptoms_to_check: Numerous small, wart-like conical or blister-like galls protruding on leaf blade surfaces.
Galled leaves curl, become crinkled, and exhibit premature chlorosis and drop.
Small exit holes on older galls indicating adult midge emergence.
immediate_actions: Prune and destroy heavily galled tender shoots before adult midges emerge.
Deep hoeing and soil solarization of the drip circle to destroy pupating cocoons in topsoil.
Maintain clean basin weed-free conditions.
preventive_measures: Conserve predatory wasps (Platygaster spp.) by avoiding non-target broad-spectrum calendar sprays.
Monitor emergence with yellow sticky cards suspended within the inner lower canopy.
treatment_options: Foliar spray with biological Beauveria bassiana (2 g/L) or Neem oil (3 ml/L) during flush emergence.
In severe recurring infestations, spray systemic Thiamethoxam (0.25 g/L) or Dimethoate (1.5 ml/L) at bud break per label instructions.
Gall Midge.when_to_seek_expert_help: Seek specialist guidance if over 50% of the flushes in establishing trees (under 5 years) are stunted by galls.

sources.title: Biology and Management of Mango Gall Midges

symptoms_to_check: Uniform rich green leaf blade free of chlorosis, necrosis, galls, and mildew coatings.
Normal flexible turgor and healthy venation pattern.
immediate_actions: No chemical intervention required.
Record scan date in orchard management log.
preventive_measures: Follow regular drip irrigation and balanced NPK + micronutrient (Zn, B, Fe) fertilization schedule.
Maintain bi-weekly scouting during critical flush, flowering, and fruit-development windows.
treatment_options: None necessary. Maintain routine protective orchard hygiene.
Healthy.when_to_seek_expert_help: Normal healthy specimen; contact extension officer only if unexplained blossom drop occurs.

symptoms_to_check: White powdery superficial fungal patches on leaves, panicles, and young fruit stems.
Affected leaves curl inward, become distorted, and turn purplish-brown before defoliating.
Drying and complete premature drop of flower buds and newly set marble-sized fruit.
immediate_actions: Inspect inflorescences and terminal vegetative flushes immediately for early white powdery spots.
Prune dense internal water sprouts to admit direct sunlight and air movement.
preventive_measures: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation during cool nights and high morning humidity periods.
Schedule preventive organic sulfur applications before full flower bloom.
treatment_options: Wettable Sulfur (2 g/L) spray at pre-bloom and post-bloom stages.
Systemic triazole fungicide such as Hexaconazole (1 ml/L) or Difenoconazole (0.5 ml/L) upon initial symptom detection.
Ensure thorough coverage of both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Powdery Mildew.when_to_seek_expert_help: Consult extension immediately if powdery patches appear on panicles during peak flowering, as yield loss can exceed 80%.

sources.title: Mango Powdery Mildew Epidemiology and Control

Sooty Mould.display_name: Mango Sooty Mould (Meliola mangiferae / Capnodium mangiferae)
symptoms_to_check: Superficial black velvety coating or crust on upper leaf surfaces, twigs, and fruit stalks.
Black film peels off in dry weather flakes or rubs off easily with water, revealing uninjured green leaf underneath.
Presence of honeydew-secreting insects (mango hoppers, mealybugs, scale insects, or aphids).
immediate_actions: Identify and treat the underlying sap-feeding insect infestation causing honeydew excretion.
Foliar wash with a 1-2% starch solution (boil 1 kg maida/flour in 5 L water, dilute to 100 L); as it dries, it flakes off the sooty film.
preventive_measures: Prune overlapping internal branches to reduce the humid sheltered conditions preferred by sap feeders.
Encourage natural predators including ladybird beetles and lacewings.
treatment_options: Target the primary insect vectors with Horticultural Spray Oil (1%) or Potassium soap (5 g/L).
If hopper population is high, apply Imidacloprid (0.3 ml/L) or Acetamiprid (0.2 g/L) per label guidance.
Sooty Mould.when_to_seek_expert_help: Seek advice if entire tree canopy is darkened and hopper population remains uncontrolled after treatment.

sources.title: Management of Mango Hoppers and Sooty Mould

symptoms_to_check: Olive-green to velvety dark brown lesions on the upper leaf surface.
Leaves become crinkled, distorted, and pucker around lesion sites.
Severe infection leads to early chlorosis and premature defoliation.
immediate_actions: Flail-mow or rake and compost fallen overwintering leaves with 5% urea spray to hasten decomposition.
Prune trees during dormancy to open canopy for rapid sun-drying of foliage.
preventive_measures: Plant scab-resistant cultivars (e.g., Enterprise, Liberty, Prima) in high-pressure regions.
Monitor Mills infection periods using weather stations (hours of leaf wetness vs temperature).
treatment_options: Protectant sprays of Mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or Captan (2 g/L) before projected rain events.
Curative systemic fungicides such as Difenoconazole (0.3 ml/L) or Myclobutanil (0.4 g/L) within 72 hours of an infection period.
scab.when_to_seek_expert_help: Contact orchard specialist if secondary scab spreads across more than 20% of terminal spur leaves.

symptoms_to_check: Bright yellow-orange or reddish circular spots on the upper leaf surface with a dark orange center.
Cluster cups (aecia) with small cylindrical projections on the leaf underside in mid-summer.
Premature leaf drop in severe seasons causing fruit sunburn and reduced return bloom.
immediate_actions: Inspect and remove gall-bearing Eastern red cedar and juniper plants within a 1-2 km radius if feasible.
Pick off and destroy localized infected leaves on small young trees.
preventive_measures: Plant rust-immune or resistant apple cultivars.
Scout nearby ornamental junipers in spring for gelatinous orange horn-like galls during wet weather.
treatment_options: Foliar fungicide applications of Myclobutanil or Mancozeb starting at pink bud through petal fall.
Ensure timely protection when cedar galls are actively sporulating during spring rains.
rust.when_to_seek_expert_help: Consult extension if defoliation exceeds 15% during early fruit sizing.

sources.title: Cedar Apple Rust on Fruit and Ornamentals

symptoms_to_check: Simultaneous presence of scab lesions, rust pustules, and fungal leaf spots (black rot or Alternaria).
Widespread leaf yellowing, marginal necrosis, and premature defoliation.
immediate_actions: Rake and safely remove all fallen orchard leaf litter immediately.
Prune dead, diseased, or cankered twigs back into healthy tissue.
preventive_measures: Implement a structured broad-spectrum integrated disease management schedule.
Improve orchard drainage and lower humidity through annual training and pruning.
treatment_options: Broad-spectrum tank mix containing a protectant (Captan 2 g/L) and a systemic triazole per regional spray guide.
Follow strict label directions and observe pre-harvest intervals.
multiple_diseases.when_to_seek_expert_help: Engage an agronomist or extension plant pathologist for a formal laboratory diagnostic culture.

symptoms_to_check: Uniform deep green leaf coloration with smooth serrated margins and no lesions or distortion.
immediate_actions: No chemical intervention needed.
Record observation in orchard monitoring ledger.
preventive_measures: Continue standard balanced fertilization and drip irrigation.
Perform routine weekly scouting for early scab or rust onset.
treatment_options: None required. Maintain standard preventive orchard sanitation.
healthy.when_to_seek_expert_help: Routine healthy foliage; consult extension if unusual wilting or fruit dropping is observed.

symptoms_to_check: Tiny dark reddish-brown to black rusty streaks parallel to leaf veins on the underside.
Streaks widen into oval sunken lesions with greyish centres and black borders.
Lesions coalesce causing large areas of leaf tissue to dry out and collapse prematurely.
immediate_actions: Deleaf severely diseased leaves (more than 50% necrotic) with a sanitized knife and place leaf face-down on soil to reduce airborne ascospore release.
Improve drainage and spacing to lower canopy relative humidity.
preventive_measures: Plant tissue-culture cultivars with known resistance to black Sigatoka where available.
Maintain optimal soil potassium levels to improve plant structural defense.
treatment_options: Systemic foliar fungicides such as Azoxystrobin, Difenoconazole, or Propiconazole mixed with mineral oil (5 L/ha) in rotation.
Apply according to local early warning disease monitoring systems to prevent resistance buildup.
Banana Black Sigatoka Disease.when_to_seek_expert_help: Consult extension if functional green leaves at flowering drop below 8 per plant.

sources.title: Management of Black Sigatoka in Banana
Sigatoka Disease Management Guide
sources.organization: Department of Agriculture and Fisheries Queensland

symptoms_to_check: Pale yellow-green narrow specks and streaks (1-2 mm) parallel to leaf veins on upper leaf surface.
Specks enlarge into elliptical spots with light ash-grey sunken centres and bright yellow halos.
Extensive blighting of mature lower leaves.
immediate_actions: Prune and remove severely affected leaf parts (surgical deleafing) to reduce inoculum.
Widen plant spacing to facilitate air movement and leaf drying.
preventive_measures: Maintain clean field sanitation and suppress weeds in planting rows.
Ensure regular balanced N and K nutrition.
treatment_options: Preventive foliar sprays of Mancozeb (2 g/L) or Chlorothalonil (2 g/L) with agricultural spray oil.
Systemic triazole fungicide during periods of high rainfall and warm temperatures.
Banana Yellow Sigatoka Disease.when_to_seek_expert_help: Consult agronomic experts if infection moves rapidly onto the youngest 3-4 leaves.

symptoms_to_check: Dark reddish-brown to chlorotic spindle-shaped streaks or mosaic stripes on leaf petioles and midribs.
Pronounced mosaic and necrotic streaks on flower bracts.
Stunted growth, leaf puckering, and choked fruit bunch emergence.
immediate_actions: Rogue and immediately eradicate infected mats (mother and suckers) using recommended systemic arboricides (e.g., glyphosate injection) to prevent sucker regrowth.
Do not harvest suckers or planting material from affected fields.
preventive_measures: Use exclusively certified virus-indexed tissue-culture plantlets for new plantations.
Monitor and control aphid vectors (Pentalonia nigronervosa).
treatment_options: No chemical cure exists for viral plant infections.
Target aphid vector control with horticultural soap or systemic insecticide before rogueing infected mats.
Banana Bract Mosaic Virus Disease.when_to_seek_expert_help: Report suspected BBrMV occurrences to state plant quarantine and extension services immediately.

sources.title: Banana Bract Mosaic Virus Technical Card

Banana Insect Pest Disease.display_name: Banana Insect Pest Damage (Weevils / Thrips / Caterpillars)
symptoms_to_check: Irregular leaf margin notches, holes, or skeletonized foliage.
Silvery scarring, rusty watermarks, or black frass specks on leaf surfaces.
Weakened pseudostem or root tunneling by banana corm weevil larvae (Cosmopolites sordidus).
immediate_actions: Inspect pseudostem base and crown leaves to identify the specific feeding insect.
Install pseudostem disc or split-log traps at ground level to monitor and capture weevils.
Remove and chop dry hanging leaves where thrips shelter.
preventive_measures: Use clean certified planting material free of weevil boreholes.
Dip planting suckers in hot water (54°C for 20 minutes) to eliminate weevil eggs and nematodes before planting.
treatment_options: Apply entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana (10^8 spores/g) or Metarhizium anisopliae around pseudostem base.
Use targeted eco-friendly Neem oil (5 ml/L) or registered bio-rational insecticides per label.
Banana Insect Pest Disease.when_to_seek_expert_help: Seek extension help if pseudostem toppling occurs due to extensive subterranean weevil boring.

sources.title: Banana Weevil Borer and Thrips Management

symptoms_to_check: Rapid yellowing, wilting, and collapse of the youngest central leaves.
Vascular bundles in pseudostem show prominent dark brown to black ring-like discoloration.
Rotting, blackened fruit with premature irregular ripening.
immediate_actions: Quarantine infected mats immediately; fence off area to avoid human, animal, or tool traffic.
Sterilize all pruning and harvesting knives in 20% sodium hypochlorite or formalin solution between every single mat.
Remove male flower buds (debudding) using a forked wooden stick to prevent insect transmission.
preventive_measures: Plant clean tissue-culture plants in fields with no history of bacterial wilt.
Establish buffer border zones and strict foot-bath biosecurity.
treatment_options: No chemical cure exists for bacterial wilt in infected tissues.
Inject diseased mats with glyphosate, allow to dry in situ, and incinerate completely.
Banana Moko Disease.when_to_seek_expert_help: Mandatory quarantine pathogen: immediately report suspected cases to the national plant protection organization.

Banana Panama Disease.display_name: Panama Disease / Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense)
symptoms_to_check: Progressive yellowing of oldest lower leaves starting from margins and moving toward midrib.
Petiole buckles at pseudostem junction, leaving a skirt of dead hanging leaves around the trunk.
Longitudinal splitting of the lower pseudostem base with red-to-dark-brown vascular strands inside.
immediate_actions: Isolate infected mat and adjacent buffer plants immediately; do not move soil, water, or tools from the site.
Disinfect footwear and machinery with quaternary ammonium compounds before leaving the field.
Destroy infected mats on site using approved containment protocols.
preventive_measures: Plant certified resistant varieties (such as GCTCV-218 or tolerant somaclones).
Maintain high soil microbial biodiversity through organic amendments and avoid flood irrigation runoff.
treatment_options: Soil-borne fungal pathogen with chlamydospores that persist 30+ years; no fungicide can cure systemic infection.
Incorporate biological control agents (Trichoderma viride, Bacillus subtilis) into soil to suppress inoculum.
Banana Panama Disease.when_to_seek_expert_help: Urgent: contact your agricultural department and university plant clinic immediately to confirm race type via molecular PCR.

symptoms_to_check: Expansive, vibrant emerald green leaf blade free of chlorotic streaks, spotting, and petiole collapse.
immediate_actions: No chemical or corrective treatment needed.
Maintain routine field observation logs.
preventive_measures: Ensure adequate potassium and nitrogen split applications to support continuous leaf emergence.
Maintain uniform soil moisture through efficient drip irrigation.
treatment_options: None required. Maintain high plantation biosecurity and sanitary tool protocols.
Banana Healthy Leaf.when_to_seek_expert_help: Healthy foliage; consult agronomist if bunch emergence or sizing problems arise.
